Subject: Private/VPC pricing & environment sizing — next steps

Hi Elena / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for taking the call this morning — appreciated the clear context on compliance and the three environments you expect (dev, staging, prod). Quick recap and a few items we promised to clarify so you have numbers for your internal finance review: 

1) Token economics reference point: based on the model mix we discussed (1x Llama2-like base for embeddings + a 7B decoder for generation), our baseline unit economics target is $1,200–$1,800 per 1M tokens for a private deployment when you include reserved capacity + support (this assumes mixed batch sizes and KV cache enabled). If you scale to sustained 2B tokens/month across environments we can pull that towards the lower end with batching and prefix caching.

2) Licensing model: Redwood Private is offered as a per-environment license with an annual fee plus optional compute overlay. For your footprint (3 envs) the licensing options are:
   - Standard: per-env license + bronze support (business hours) — recommended if you want predictable cost and lighter SLAs.
   - Enterprise: per-env license + silver/gold support (24/7 critical incident) — includes runbook integrations, audit log retention options, and SLA credits.

3) Support tier pricing: ballpark multipliers we use for quoting: bronze = +0% to base license, silver = +18% license, gold = +35% license (gold also includes faster escalation paths and named CSM). We can produce exact numbers once you confirm environment count and retention windows.

4) Environment sizing: for your stated concurrency (peak ~120 concurrent users across prod) and throughput (avg 10M tokens/day), recommended footprint is: 2x 8-GPU nodes for prod, 1x 4-GPU for staging, 1x 4-GPU for dev (we can right-size after a 2-week pilot). Pricing sheet attached shows per-node pricing and an option with reserved capacity discounts.

Next steps / asks:
- Can you confirm the number of canonical environments (you mentioned a possibility of an additional "pre-prod" env). If you want pre-prod + prod + staging + dev that changes license count.
- Can you share a ballpark monthly token volume range (min / target / max) for the first 12 months so we can give a 1M-token blended target price?
- Which support tier do you typically require for regulated workloads (Acme procurement preferences)?

I've attached an initial pricing sheet and a draft SOW template for your legal team to review. I can also run a quick ROI slide showing $/1M-token sensitivity across volumes if that helps your CFO.

If it's helpful, I'm happy to join your internal procurement call next Wed — let me know.

Thanks,

--

Thanks Marissa — very helpful summary. Two quick clarifications from our side: 

1) Token volumes: rough ballpark for year 1 we expect 200M tokens/month as a midpoint, but during pilot months could be as low as 50M and spike to 500M in marketing events. Our CFO wants to see an expected $/1M token figure we can model against both 200M and 500M.

2) Environments: we will likely need four canonical environments (dev, test/staging, pre-prod, prod). We may consolidate dev into a smaller shared env but budget reviewers prefer counting four.

Procurement note: our security team requires SOC2 evidence and an option for customer-managed KMS. We saw those in Redwood docs but will need confirmation in the SOW.

Would a follow-up with pricing that shows 200M and 500M monthly scenarios work?

—Elena

Marissa / Elena — quick technical + pricing clarifications from my side: 

- The 1,200–1,800 per 1M tokens Marissa mentioned assumes: mixed model usage, 16-bit quantization variants where appropriate, and a 12-month reserved capacity contract for the prod pool. If Acme wants month-to-month for pilot months, expect a ~25% premium on unit economics for that period.

- For multi-env pricing, we typically offer a 10% bundle discount on the 2nd and 3rd env licenses and a 15% discount on 4+ envs when the same customer signs up across environments at once (this is in lieu of per-node discounts). That should help with four-env math.

- Support tier note: gold includes 8-hour on-call SLA for Sev1 and a named escalation engineer; silver is 12-hour and bronze is next-business-day. If compliance requires SOC2 + customer-managed KMS, customer must sign the enterprise SOW we attached which includes SOC2 evidence and KMS integration options.

I'll prepare two scenario sheets: 200M tokens/month and 500M tokens/month with expected $/1M-token at baseline and at pilot month premium. Marissa — I'll need the final environment count to lock numbers.

Jonas
Principal Solutions Architect
